content.title: About
content.content: Multigrain restructured potato chips are a light, crunchy snack made from whole potatoes, whole grains (oats, corn, rice) and a small amount of plant protein. The restructuring technology binds the ingredients into a single matrix, preserving the classic potato flavor while adding the nutritional benefits of grains.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Restructured chips contain up to 30 % whole grains, increasing fiber compared with regular potato chips.
The technology reduces the amount of added oil without sacrificing crispness.
The multigrain blend often includes oats, which are rich in beta‑glucan – a soluble fiber beneficial for heart health.
Chips are made without artificial flavors or colorings; taste comes from natural potato aroma and light toasting of the grains.
In some countries these chips are classified as a “semi‑finished product,” simplifying import procedures.

items.title: Higher fiber content
items.content: Whole grains boost dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Low trans‑fat levels
items.content: Restructuring allows the use of plant oils low in trans fats, which is heart‑friendly.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Oats and corn provide slow‑release energy, helping maintain satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Grains supply thiamine, niacin, and folate, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Potato and oat polyphenols help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Grain allergies
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to oats, corn, or rice and should avoid the product.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Like most chips, it can contain a notable amount of salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite reduced oil, the snack remains energy‑dense and can contribute to weight gain if over‑consumed.

items.title: Gluten presence
items.content: If oats are included, the product may contain trace gluten, important for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the chips straight from the bag, toss them into salads for crunch, use as a garnish for soups, or serve with dips such as yogurt‑based sauces, guacamole, or hummus.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the chips in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, transfer to an airtight container to maintain crispness.
